chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from more than one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

We said to him: 'Is the Sufyani inevitable?' He said: 'Yes, and the killing of the pure soul is inevitable, and the Rising (of the Mahdi) is inevitable, and the sinking of the Baida' is inevitable, and the hand appearing from the sky is inevitable, and the call from the sky is inevitable.' I said: 'And what will the call be?' He said: 'A caller will call out the name of the Rising (al-Qa'im) and the name of his father.'

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: The Sufyani, a key figure in Shia eschatology who rises before the Mahdi
key_terms.النَّفْسُ الزَّكِيَّةُ: The Pure Soul, referring to a specific martyr killed before the Mahdi's appearance
key_terms.النِّدَاءُ: The call, a divine announcement from the sky
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser, a title for the Mahdi
key_terms.خَسْفُ الْبَيْدَاءَ: The sinking of the Baida', a miraculous event in the desert of Mecca
key_terms.كَفُّ طُلُوعٍ: The hand appearing, a sign from the sky

ai.seo_question: What are the inevitable signs preceding the appearance of the Mahdi according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* confirms the inevitability (*al-mahmum*) of key eschatological events, linking the Sufyani’s rise and the Khuruj of the Mahdi to specific cosmic and terrestrial signs like the *Kasf* (lifting of the sky) and *Khasf* (sinking of the desert). It highlights the unique role of the celestial call (*Nida’*) in publicly identifying the Mahdi by name and his father’s lineage, a detail often associated with the year 260 AH in Shia historiography. This establishes the Mahdi’s appearance not as a sudden surprise but as a divinely ordained sequence of confirmed signs.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (15) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ali bin al-Hasan from Ya’qoob bin Zayd from Ziyad al-Qandi from some of his companions that it was said to Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as):

“Is the rising of as-Sufyani inevitable?” He said: “Yes, it is. Killing the pure innocent man, the sinking of the desert, the appearance of a hand in the sky, the call that comes from the Heaven and the appearance of al-Qa’im are also inevitable.” It was said to him: “What is the call?” He said: “A caller calling out the name of al-Qa’im and the name of his father (as).”
